topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

outline.topic: Proof of Snell's Law: The Principle of Least Time

sections.title: Hook & Intuition: The Lifeguard Problem
sections.content: Introduce the physical intuition behind refraction. Use the analogy of a lifeguard on a beach who must reach a swimmer in the water. Since running on sand is faster than swimming in water, the lifeguard chooses a path that minimizes time, not distance.
sections.example: Visualize a lifeguard path: The path bends at the shoreline to stay on the 'faster' sand for a longer duration.

sections.title: Fermat’s Principle & Prerequisites
sections.content: Define Fermat’s Principle of Least Time: Light follows the path that takes the minimum time. Define indices of refraction (n1, n2) and velocity (v1=c/n1, v2=c/n2). Prepare the geometry: a light ray crossing from medium 1 to medium 2 at point P(x, y).
sections.example: A diagram showing two coordinate systems with an interface at y=0, showing distance L1 in medium 1 and L2 in medium 2.

sections.title: Mathematical Derivation
sections.content: Set up the total time function T(x) = (distance1/v1) + (distance2/v2). Express distance using the Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(a^2 + x^2)/v1 + sqrt(b^2 + (w-x)^2)/v2. Explain that to find the minimum, we set the derivative dT/dx = 0.
sections.example: Animation showing the dynamic calculation of time as the entry point x moves along the interface.

sections.title: Synthesizing Snell’s Law
sections.content: Solving dT/dx = 0 results in (x/v1)/sqrt(a^2 + x^2) = ((w-x)/v2)/sqrt(b^2 + (w-x)^2). Identify these ratios as sin(θ1)/v1 = sin(θ2)/v2. Substituting v=c/n leads to n1*sin(θ1) = n2*sin(θ2).
sections.example: Final slide showing the transformation from the calculus equation to the elegant trigonometric identity of Snell's Law.

sections.title: Conclusion & Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize that refraction isn't just a geometric rule, but a consequence of nature optimizing travel time. Reiterate that this logic applies to fiber optics, lenses, and even mirages.
sections.example: A short animation of a laser pulse through a glass block, pausing to highlight the angle changes at the interface.
